title: Finance blueprint passes tenant-wide mail and SharePoint read to an email-triggered agent
risk_statement: Because the Finance Agents Blueprint (bp-finance) passes tenant-wide application Mail.Read (all mailboxes incl. CFO) and Sites.Read.All (all sites) to every child identity, and agent-invoice runs as ai-invoice-01 while autonomously processing untrusted external email, an external sender could use indirect prompt injection to make the agent read and disclose mail or documents far beyond the invoices mailbox, resulting in tenant-wide loss of confidential executive and finance data.
likelihood_rationale: Untrusted external email is processed autonomously with generative orchestration on; sending an email takes minimal effort; no content filter, prompt shield or human approval is evidenced. Not 5 because a disclosure channel is not evidenced (Post to ERP API scope unknown).
impact_rationale: Grants are app-only and tenant-wide over two critical assets (all mailboxes incl. CFO; all SharePoint sites); tool blast-radius score 35, or 39 if the blueprint credential leaks.
recommended_action: Replace tenant-wide grants with resource-scoped access: limit mail access to the invoices shared mailbox (Exchange Online RBAC for Applications or an application access policy) and replace Sites.Read.All with Sites.Selected on the Finance site. Stop granting high-privilege permissions at blueprint level so children do not inherit them. Add prompt-injection defences and human approval before ERP posts. Confirm the ERP API scope.
owner: TBD (suggest: Finance Applications Owner, with Entra Identity Administrator)

title: HR Benefits Assistant gives anonymous internet users access to HR-Confidential via maker credentials
risk_statement: Because agent-hr-benefits is published to the public website with no user authentication and reads employee records through a SharePoint connection that runs with its maker's credentials, any anonymous internet user could query the agent to retrieve Highly Confidential HR content, resulting in a personal-data breach with regulatory, legal and reputational consequences.
likelihood_rationale: Internet-facing and anonymous; shortest attack path in the model (2 hops); no attacker effort beyond chatting; no compensating control evidenced.
impact_rationale: HR-Confidential is labelled Highly Confidential and critical; maker credentials bypass per-user access checks. Breadth is one site in the model; wider reach of the maker's own access is not evidenced.
recommended_action: Remove the public website channel now or enforce Entra ID authentication. Replace the maker-credential connection with end-user (delegated) authentication so SharePoint permissions apply per user. Give the agent a dedicated Entra agent identity. Confirm business need (no activity for 50 days) and unpublish if not needed.

title: Helpdesk agent can reset other users' passwords for any employee who asks
risk_statement: Because agent-helpdesk runs as ai-helpdesk-01 holding the Entra Helpdesk Administrator role, offers password-reset and unlock tools to any authenticated employee in Teams, and no caller verification or approval step is evidenced, a malicious insider or a compromised employee account could instruct the agent to reset another user's password, resulting in account takeover and onward access to that user's data (in the model, critical payroll storage via user-dana).
assets: agent-helpdesk; ai-helpdesk-01; bp-itops; role-helpdesk-admin; user-dana; st-payroll
likelihood_rationale: Reachable by every authenticated employee, so any one compromised account suffices; generative orchestration with a direct reset tool; no caller verification, human approval or guardrail evidenced.
impact_rationale: Directory role allows reset of non-admin users; modelled reach is one user leading to critical payroll storage (blast-radius score 20). Breadth beyond user-dana is not modelled.
recommended_action: Remove the standing Helpdesk Administrator role from ai-helpdesk-01 or scope it with an administrative unit. Limit the reset tool to the authenticated caller's own account, or require target-user re-verification and human approval for resets of others. Log and alert on agent-initiated resets. Confirm where the bp-itops credential is stored.
owner: TBD (suggest: IT Service Desk Manager, with Entra Identity Administrator)

title: Finance blueprint secret is stored in an ops vault the DevOps agent can read
risk_statement: Because the finance blueprint's client secret is stored in kv-contoso-ops, where the DevOps Copilot's managed identity holds Key Vault Secrets User and the agent has a Key Vault get secret tool, anyone who controls the DevOps agent or its identity could read the secret and request tokens for all three finance agent identities, resulting in escalation from platform tooling to tenant-wide mailbox and SharePoint read access.
assets: kv-contoso-ops; secret-bp-finance; bp-finance; mi-agent-devops; ai-invoice-01; ai-invoice-02; ai-expense-01
likelihood_rationale: Requires control of the DevOps agent or its identity; the modelled entry (compromised developer workstation) is an assumed-breach scenario, not an observed event. Once there, no further privilege is needed. Other vault readers, rotation and access policy are not evidenced.
impact_rationale: One credential unlocks three identities with tenant-wide Mail.Read and Sites.Read.All (blueprint blast-radius score 39); secret-bp-finance sits on 4 of 11 attack paths.
recommended_action: Move the finance blueprint credential to a finance-owned vault with no DevOps access. Prefer a certificate or federated credential over a client secret. Rotate the secret now because another team's identity could read it. Scope Key Vault RBAC to the specific secrets the DevOps agent needs. List every principal with read access to kv-contoso-ops.
owner: TBD (suggest: Cloud Platform Lead, with Finance Applications Owner)

title: DevOps Copilot holds standing Contributor and run-command power over production
risk_statement: Because the DevOps Copilot runs as mi-agent-devops with standing Contributor on rg-production and offers Run command on VM and Azure Resource Manager tools, a stolen developer session or manipulated agent instructions could drive the agent to run code on or change production resources, resulting in compromise of the payroll database VM and production disruption.
likelihood_rationale: Entry needs a stolen Teams session or Foundry project access (assumed-breach node); on-behalf-of user authentication adds some binding. But the agent is the top choke point (6 of 11 paths) and no approval step is evidenced.
impact_rationale: Contributor over production including the critical payroll DB VM; largest blast radius in the model (12 nodes, 4 critical, score 74).
recommended_action: Remove standing Contributor; use just-in-time elevation (PIM for Azure resources) or a least-action custom role. Require human approval for Run command and other write actions. Separate read-only diagnostic tools from change tools. Require phishing-resistant MFA and a compliant device for developer access to the agent.

title: AI agent ownership and lifecycle not managed (one agent already orphaned)
risk_statement: Because each agent has a single owner, no owner or sponsor is recorded for agent identities, blueprints, the managed identity or the maker connection, and no joiner-mover-leaver link is evidenced, agents and their privileges could stay live after the owner leaves or the need ends, resulting in access nobody answers for or remediates. This has already happened: agent-marketing is Published, owned only by a disabled account and inactive for 255 days.
assets: agent-marketing; agent-hr-benefits; agent-invoice; agent-devops; agent-helpdesk; ai-invoice-01; ai-invoice-02; ai-expense-01; ai-helpdesk-01; mi-agent-devops; bp-finance; bp-itops; conn-maker-alex
likelihood_rationale: Evidenced: 1 of 5 published agents is already orphaned; every agent has one owner; identity objects have no owner fields. Not 5 because the other four owners are not in the disabled list (active status inferred only).
impact_rationale: The orphaned agent itself has low reach (no tools or identity, public knowledge, blast-radius score 2, 0 attack paths). The same gap covers identities and blueprints with tenant-wide and production privileges, where lost ownership would leave High risks unremediated.
recommended_action: Assign a primary owner, backup owner and business sponsor to every agent, agent identity, blueprint, managed identity and connection. Link agent ownership to the HR leaver process. Unpublish or reassign agent-marketing. Review the other four agents (49-51 days without activity) for continued need.

title: Monitoring and detection of agent activity not evidenced
risk_statement: Because no audit logging, diagnostic settings, Defender or Sentinel alerting, conversation transcripts or prompt-injection detection is evidenced for any agent or agent identity, misuse such as bulk mailbox reads, agent-initiated password resets or secret retrieval could go undetected, resulting in late response and a larger breach.
assets: All 5 agents; ai-invoice-01; ai-invoice-02; ai-expense-01; ai-helpdesk-01; mi-agent-devops; kv-contoso-ops
likelihood_rationale: PROVISIONAL. The model has no monitoring fields, so coverage is unknown rather than proven absent. Scored at the midpoint pending the evidence request.
impact_rationale: Detection is the main compensating control for R-01 to R-05; without it tenant-wide and production misuse would run unchecked. Not 5 because missing detection amplifies loss rather than causing it.
recommended_action: Evidence request first: show logging and alerting coverage for each agent and identity. If absent: enable sign-in and audit logs for agent identities, Key Vault diagnostic logs and agent transcript logging, and alert on secret reads, app-only bulk mail reads and agent-initiated password resets.

title: Finance agent identities with tenant-wide grants but no inventoried agent
risk_statement: Because ai-invoice-02 and ai-expense-01 hold tenant-wide application permissions (Mail.Read on all mailboxes; Sites.Read.All on all sites) through bp-finance but no inventoried agent runs as them, they could be used by an unknown workload or by anyone holding the blueprint credential, resulting in tenant-wide data access outside any agent's governance.
likelihood_rationale: No consumer is evidenced; the only modelled way to use them is the bp-finance credential (scored in R-04). No activity data, so unused status is unconfirmed.
impact_rationale: Tenant-wide app-only access to two critical assets.
recommended_action: Check sign-in logs for both identities. If unused, remove their permissions and delete them. If used, add the consuming agent to the inventory and assign an owner.

title: Exposure analyzer and data classification can under-report risk
risk_statement: Because the lab exposure analyzer flags only application, Owner or Contributor grants, truncates choke points to five, uses a fixed inactivity cut-off date, and the Finance SharePoint knowledge source is labelled Confidential but not critical, material exposures could be missed or under-ranked in routine reporting, resulting in mis-prioritised remediation.
likelihood_rationale: Already observed in this run: Key Vault Secrets User grant not flagged; secret-bp-finance (on 4 paths) hidden by truncation; inactivity check fixed at 2026-06-01.
impact_rationale: Does not expose data by itself; weakens prioritisation of the High risks. Applies to the lab analyzer; Defender XDR behaviour is not evidenced.
recommended_action: Flag Key Vault data-plane roles and directory roles; show all choke points including ties; compute inactivity from the run date; decide whether kn-finance-sharepoint should be critical; check whether Defender XDR exposure output has the same limits.
